features.entity_name: JUNO underground experimental hall, Dashi Hill, Kaiping
features.method: Coordinate published by the JUNO Collaboration (arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2, repeated in arXiv:1507.05613 Sec. 1.3.1): 112°31'05" E, 22°07'05" N converted to decimal degrees as 112 + 31/60 + 5/3600 and 22 + 7/60 + 5/3600. Arc-second rounding alone is ~21 m; accuracy_m is set to 150 m because the same paper states the hall was moved ~60 m from its design position, does not say which position the quoted coordinate describes or its datum, and the published core baselines imply a position ~100 m SSW of this point (see notes).

provenance.locator: arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2 "JUNO experimental site"; arXiv:1507.05613 Sec. 1.3.1 "Experimental site"
provenance.note: Representation is 'surveyed' (coordinate published by the collaboration) but confidence is kept 'approximate': the coordinate carries arc-second rounding, a stated ~60 m design shift and an ~100 m disagreement with the baselines (see notes).
provenance.quote: The geographic location is 112° 31’05” E and 22° 07’05” N.

summary.plain: The JUNO neutrino detector sits in a rock hall under Dashi Hill near Kaiping, in southern China. This map shows the hall's published position and the surface campus; the two reactor complexes it listens to are on the linked baseline map.

unlocated.backlog: The JUNO civil-engineering drawings (CDR Figs. 10.3 and 10.4 are unscaled), the JUNO TDR / detector-construction paper civil chapter, or a Chinese environmental-impact assessment giving shaft-collar coordinates; failing that an OSM feature for the Dongkeng quarry shaft or the portal. With the portal coordinate the inclined shaft can be drawn as a line (horizontal run = 1266 m x cos(atan 0.425)).
unlocated.reason: The two access routes to the hall are described only by length and slope: a vertical shaft 564 m deep (arXiv:2104.02565; 581 m in the CDR, 589 m in its geology chapter) in the Dongkeng quarry, joined to the hall by a 300 m tunnel at 3 % slope, and an inclined tunnel 1266 m long at 42.5 % slope (CDR: 1,340 m at 42.6 %, entrance portal at Shenghe Village, Jinji Town) with an 85 m interconnecting tunnel. No fetched source gives a coordinate, bearing or surveyed plan for either, and OpenStreetMap carries neither a quarry nor a portal or shaft feature there (only the research-campus outline). Drawing them would mean inventing a bearing.
